Images per optimizer step. Higher batches smooth gradients but cost more VRAM.
Optimizer steps accumulated before an update — multiplies the effective batch size without extra VRAM.

What the run trains. LoRA is the standard low-rank adapter; LoKr (LyCORIS Kronecker) trains a much smaller, often more expressive adapter on targets that advertise it; Full base fine-tune updates every base weight and writes a fine-tuned checkpoint instead of an adapter — far more memory, offered only where the engine supports it.
Learning-rate scheduler (not the timestep/noise scheduler). Constant holds the LR fixed for the whole run; linear and cosine decay it toward zero over the run.
Optional linear warmup: number of steps to ramp the LR up from zero before the scheduler body runs. 0 disables warmup.
Perturb the adapter weights with small seeded noise after every optimizer step (relative to each tensor's RMS) — a regularizer against overfitting a small character dataset. Off by default.
Seeded Gaussian adapter-gradient noise: eta / (1 + step)^gamma. Helps escape poor early minima. Off by default.

Train every image at several resolutions with square rows, or explicitly choose width × height rows to assign images by closest aspect. Each row has its own repeat count per epoch. Replaces the single Resolution above. Off by default.
